name: Walkies: Explore Your Suburb
subtitle: Clear the clouds by walking
_category: Health & Fitness first: it's a reason to get out for a walk and it counts your steps, and that's where people looking for a walking app browse. Lifestyle second, for exploring your neighbourhood and its local history. Not Navigation: it never gives directions, and a reviewer expecting routing would be confused.
promotionalText: I built this to make walking the dog a bit more interesting. Your suburb starts off under clouds and they clear as you walk, so the idea is to get it all to 100%.
description:
I built Walkies to make walking the dog a bit more interesting. Your suburb starts off under clouds on a satellite map and they clear off the tiles as you walk through them, so the idea is to try and get it all to 100%. It's a lot harder than it sounds, and a good excuse to go down all the streets you'd normally never bother with.

The tiles are about 87 metres across around Perth, and only the ones with a street or path you can walk on count, so you're never stuck needing to swim across a lake. The streets are dotted over the clouds so you can plan where to head next. Bikes and cars don't count either, so no clearing your suburb from the car window. Walking and jogging do, as long as you're under about 12 km/h.

There's secrets hidden under some of the tiles too. Around Busselton in Western Australia there's 136 of them spread across about 30 suburbs, mostly little bits of local history with some Wardandi Noongar heritage and nature mixed in. You don't know where they are, so you've got to go out and explore, and when you walk over one it goes in your secrets book with its own sticker. If you live somewhere else you still get the clouds and the tiles, just no secrets yet. Hopefully I can add some more places over time.

When you finish a walk it plays back over the map, with your route drawing itself and the clouds popping off each new tile, then it has a guess at how many more walks like it you'll need to finish the suburb. Every walk is kept with its route, distance, time and steps, so you can go back and watch any of them again.

I've gamified it a bit too. You get shells for new tiles, finding secrets, walking a few days in a row and doing the three quests you get each week, and you can spend them in the Shop on things like a different marker for you on the map, cloud colours, or a spyglass that puts a ring on the map somewhere around a secret you haven't found yet. They add up to levels as well, and every level lets you pick a reward.

If you give Walkies "Always" location access it notices when you head out on foot and records the walk by itself, then ends it once you've stopped for ten minutes. That's up to you though, you can switch it off in Settings and just press Start walk when you go.

You can add the suburbs next door with one tap, and start a team with up to eight people. It all works without signal too: everything's saved on your phone first and backed up to your account whenever it can, so if you get a new phone you just sign in with Apple or Google and it all comes back. There's no ads and nothing's sold to anyone.

The idea came from my mate James, who told me about a walking app he'd been working on where you try and walk every single street in your city. I never actually got to see it, and I got too impatient, so I made my own. If you find a bug or have an idea, tap "Suggest a feature" in Settings or email me at walkies@mikecann.app. Hopefully you like it!

ageRating._note: Walkies has no objectionable content: a map, your walks, and short local-history stories. The only things anyone else sees are a team's name and its members' names and colours (invite-only), and feature requests from Suggest a feature once Mike has approved them, without who sent them. So userGeneratedContent is false, the same as Poddle. healthOrWellnessTopics is false too: it counts steps but gives no health advice. Apple's newer questions the script can't answer yet (socialMedia, socialMediaAgeRestricted) are answered in App Store Connect: no social media. Unknown keys are skipped, and keys Apple adds later are left as they are.

review.notes:
Thanks for taking a look at Walkies.

SIGNING IN
Sign-up is open to anyone, so there's no demo account. Tap "Sign in with Apple" or "Sign in with Google" on the first screen with your own Apple or Google account and you get a new, empty Walkies account of your own.

THE FIRST RUN
After signing in, a short setup asks for location (with Motion & Fitness), then notifications, and says what each is for before iOS asks.
- Location "Always" is optional. It's only for Always on (Settings > Always on), which notices when you head out on foot and records the walk by itself, then ends it after ten minutes without moving. With "While Using the App", or with Always on switched off, everything else works the same and you tap Start walk on the map to record a walk. The location background mode is there so a walk you started keeps recording with the phone locked in a pocket.
- Motion & Fitness tells walking from cycling or driving, and counts steps.
- Notifications are local only: a secret found while the phone's in a pocket.

TRYING IT WITHOUT WALKING A WHOLE SUBURB
1. Tap the place name at the top left of the map (it says "Places" until you've added one), then "Add a place", and search for any suburb or town, for example Cupertino. Its outline and streets come from OpenStreetMap, and it turns up under clouds split into hex tiles, with the streets dotted over the top. The first time anyone adds a place it can take up to a minute.
2. Switch off Settings > Always on, so the map has a Start walk button. Tap it and walk a little way down a street outside (a minute or two is plenty). The tiles you walk through clear. Anything over about 12 km/h, or in a car, doesn't count. In the Simulator, Features > Location > City Walk does the same.
3. Tap End walk to see the replay of the walk and the tiles it cleared. It's then in the Walks tab, and the Progress tab shows the shells and levels it earned.
Without going outside at all, you can still add a place and see it under the clouds, and look through the Secrets, Progress (levels, quests and the Shop) and Settings tabs.

SECRETS
The secrets are only around Busselton, Western Australia for now, so anywhere else the Secrets book shows them all as not found yet. Everything else works anywhere.

DELETING THE ACCOUNT
Settings > Delete account. It asks twice, then deletes the account and everything in it from the server, clears the phone and signs out.

OTHER
- "Suggest a feature" in Settings is a feedback form. The microphone and speech recognition are only used if you record a voice note there.
- Teams are invite-only. Members see each other's name and colour (and Google photo), never each other's walks.
- No ads, no tracking and no in-app purchases. Shells are earned by walking and can't be bought.
